thread:
maria: heads up — noticed a lot of scale-flap in ap-southeast this morning. cluster-autoscaler keeps adding then almost immediately removing gpu nodes for batch-inference jobs. cost spike and failed startups.
ian: yup saw that in the dashboard. pods get scheduled, then some go Pending because init containers hit our registry egress quota, CA thinks nodes are idle and marks them unneeded.
ashok: are we still using the default --scale-down-unneeded-time? that seems aggressive for spot mixes.
maria: we were at 5m. I think combination of preemptible nodes + network egress throttles is causing transient unneeded decisions.
jenks: proposal: increase scale-down thresholds and add a staggered launch window so CA waits longer before considering recently added nodes unneeded. also bump max-node-provision-time so long startup doesn't trigger scale-down.
ian: sounds reasonable. concretely what flags are we thinking?
maria: rough draft:
```
--scale-down-unneeded-time=15m
--scale-down-unready-time=20m
--scale-down-delay-after-add=12m
--max-node-provision-time=18m
--expander=least-waste
--balance-similar-node-groups=true
```
ian: +1 to least-waste for our heterogeneous pools. it reduces overprovisioning when GPUs come in different sizes.
ashok: also consider --skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false? some of our TFServing pods write checkpoints to local scratch during startup and CA counts them as evictable incorrectly.
jenks: hmm risky but worth testing in a canary cluster. we should also add a cheap fallback: make a small dedicated warm pool (2 nodes) in the most impacted AZs so short bursts don't trigger new provisioning. cheaper than constant scale churn.
maria: agree on canary. i'll spin up a canary cluster in ap-southeast with those flags and a 2-node warm pool (spot + reserved mix). will run synthetic traffic for 2 days.
sre-bot: deploy scheduled: canary-autoscaler-tune -> ap-southeast-canary at 2026-03-20T09:40Z by maria
ian: callout — we should monitor three metrics during test: node add latency, CA scale-down decisions per node, and failed pod starts due to egress. add alerts if scale-down rate > 1/min sustained for 10m.
maria: noted. I'll post results and a diff for the CA helm chart after the run. thanks all :thumbsup:
jenks: if test looks good, plan a phased rollout to prod with per-region rollbacks. prefer staged because eu-west has different spot dynamics.
ashok: also log the eviction-reason and include kubelet logs for nodes marked unneeded; that helped root-cause last time.
maria: will attach logs. closing loop in this thread after canary completes.
